title: Agents are the new SaaS: a playbook for finding, building and selling agents as labor
summary: Greg argues the product is the job, not the tool, and that selling work targets a labor market far bigger than software. He walks through picking a paid workflow, shadowing humans, building a minimal useful agent, adding a trust wrapper and evals, selling pilots, outcome pricing, tear-down content, and a 30-day plan.

principles.text: Sell the job, not the tool: agent SaaS sells work the customer no longer does by hand.
principles.quote: SAS sells software agent SAS sells work.

principles.text: Start with a workflow that already has a paycheck attached, then sell it cheaper than the employee or agency doing it.
principles.quote: You want to start with the paycheck, right? If people are already paying for the work, they're paying an employee, they're paying an agency, a receptionist, a coordinator, dispatcher

principles.text: Shadow a human doing the job 10 to 20 times before you build; the detail is the product.
principles.quote: you actually want to shadow the human before you build.

principles.text: Build the smallest useful agent (draft and approve, triage, coordinate, bounded action) and earn autonomy over time.
principles.quote: Founders should earn autonomy by starting with a predictable path and adding judgment only when it creates value.

principles.text: Sell pilots to a few customers in one niche, charge setup plus monthly, then productize repeated patterns. Move toward outcome pricing as you learn the value.
principles.quote: you earn the software by doing the work first.

principles.text: Distribute with workflow tear-downs: show the old painful way versus the agent way, and own one workflow in content.
principles.quote: Pick one workflow, make the internet associate you with it.
